newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's Horn accepts welfare minister resignation.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's Horn accepts welfare minister resignation.

text.p: Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn accepted Welfare Minister Gyorgy Szabo's resignation, officials said on Monday, but a successor has not been named.

Szabo, who tendered his resignation over two weeks ago, has declined to give any reason for the move, triggering media speculation about a cabinet dispute over financing Hungary's crumbling welfare system.
"Following a discussion this morning, the prime minister will initiate dismissal procedures with President Arpad Goncz as of November 30," government spokesman Elemer Kiss told Hungarian television.
Horn asked Szabo to stay in office for two weeks after he handed in his resignation on November 6.
Szabo is the ninth minister to resign from Horn's coalition government of Socialists and Free Democrats since it was formed in May 1994. All but one have been appointees from Horn's Socialist Party.
